intended_object: The restriction map Γ(A, U) = ⨁ₙ Γ(Aₙ, U) → ⨁ₙ Γ(Aₙ, V) for opens V ⊆ U, where A = ⨁ₙ Aₙ is an ℕ-graded commutative 𝒪_X-algebra on a scheme X. It is a degree-preserving ring homomorphism that restricts each homogeneous component. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body uses `DirectSum.toSemiring` to build a ring homomorphism. Its component in degree n sends a section x of Aₙ over U to its restriction `(A.X n).presheaf.map f.op x`, placed in degree n. The required facts that restriction preserves the unit and the graded multiplication are proved by naturality. By `restrictGradedSections_apply`, the map restricts each component, so it is the direct sum of the restriction maps. This is exactly the standard restriction map of the graded ring of sections, and it is functorial (`restrictGradedSections_id` and `restrictGradedSections_comp`).

The ℕ-grading is the one fixed throughout the library's setup, and it is the standard grading for graded algebras on schemes, which feed relative Proj. Mathlib has no general version of this construction for sheaves of graded algebras on schemes, so the definition is not too narrow.
